notes: Not obfuscated - this file is already a clean, hand-written/rewritten bignum implementation (doc comment header, no 'Decompiled by JODE' banner, meaningful names throughout) unlike the other files in this batch. Private primary constructor takes the sign-magnitude representation directly; params already clearly named, no rename needed.
Constructs from a big-endian two's-complement signed byte array (java.math.BigInteger(byte[]) semantics), delegating to fromSignedBytes(value). Already clearly named.
Constructs a positive value from a hex string; only radix 16 is supported (asserted via require). Already clearly named.
Returns the big-endian two's-complement minimal-length byte encoding, matching java.math.BigInteger.toByteArray(). Already correctly named.
True when the magnitude array is empty (the canonical zero representation used throughout, since stripLeadingZeros/of never leave a nonzero-sign empty-mag pair). Already correctly named.

Standard square-and-multiply modular exponentiation (LSB-first over exp's bits via testBit0/shiftRight1), reducing the base into [0, m) first via mod(). Used for RSA-style login/JS5 crypto per the file's doc comment. Already correctly named.
this * o mod m, a private helper combining multiply() and mod(). Already correctly named; only the param name `o` could be marginally clearer as `other`.
Returns true if the least-significant bit of the magnitude is 1 (checks mag[last limb] and 1). Already correctly named.
Arithmetic right shift of the (non-negative) magnitude by 1 bit, propagating the carry bit between 32-bit limbs; returns ZERO for zero input. Already correctly named.

Schoolbook long multiplication of the two magnitudes (double-loop with 64-bit accumulator/carry), sign = sign * o.sign. Already correctly named; `o` could be renamed `other` for clarity but is unambiguous in context.
Non-negative remainder matching java.math.BigInteger.mod(m): takes the truncated remainder() and adds m back if it came out negative. Already correctly named.
Truncated remainder (sign follows the dividend, like BigInteger.remainder) - compares magnitudes and calls divRemMag when a real division is needed. Already correctly named.

Sign-magnitude addition supporting same-sign (magnitude add) and opposite-sign (magnitude subtract of the larger from the smaller, keeping the larger's sign) cases - the specific subset needed by mod(). Already correctly named; `o` could be `other`.
Companion factory that strips leading-zero limbs and canonicalizes to the shared ZERO instance when the magnitude is empty. Already correctly named.
Trims leading zero limbs from a big-endian limb array, returning the same array reference when nothing to trim. Already correctly named.
Unsigned comparison of two magnitude limb arrays (by length first, then limb-by-limb as unsigned 32-bit values). Already correctly named.
Unsigned addition of two magnitude limb arrays with carry propagation, output sized to the larger operand + 1 limb then trimmed. Already correctly named.
Unsigned subtraction a - b of magnitude limb arrays (requires a >= b) with borrow propagation. Already correctly named.

Binary long division of magnitudes bit-by-bit (shift-and-subtract), returning (quotient, remainder) as a Pair; requires a >= b, b != 0. Intentionally simple per the file's doc comment since RSA blocks here are only 64-128 bytes. Already correctly named.
Reads a single bit (indexed from the least-significant bit) out of a big-endian limb array; out-of-range (limb < 0) returns 0. Already correctly named.
Sets a single bit (indexed from the least-significant bit) in a big-endian limb array in place. Already correctly named.

Left-shifts a magnitude by 1 bit and ORs `lowBit` into the new least-significant bit position, growing the array by one limb if needed then trimming. Used by divRemMag to build up the running remainder one bit at a time. Already correctly named.
Parses a hex string into a big-endian 32-bit limb array, left-padding with zeros to a multiple of 8 hex digits (one limb) first. Already correctly named.

Decodes a big-endian two's-complement byte array (java.math.BigInteger(byte[]) semantics) into (sign, magnitude): for negative inputs it computes the two's-complement magnitude via bitwise-invert + 1 over the byte array before converting to limbs. Already correctly named.
Converts a big-endian byte array (already sign-resolved, non-two's-complement) into a big-endian 32-bit limb array, skipping leading zero bytes. Already correctly named.

Inverse of fromSignedBytes: encodes (sign, magnitude) into a minimal-length big-endian two's-complement byte array matching java.math.BigInteger.toByteArray(), including the extra leading 0x00/0xff byte needed when the magnitude's top bit would otherwise flip the encoded sign. Already correctly named.
